description: :tophat: simple, fun and transparent SSH (and telnet) bastion server

summary.one_liner: A transparent SSH (and telnet) bastion server in Go that lets users reach remote hosts through a single portal without modifying their SSH clients.
summary.what_it_does: sshportal runs as a single binary that embeds an SSH server and client, so users connect to it and are routed to configured remote hosts. It manages hosts, host groups, users, user groups, SSH keys and ACLs, and includes an invite system so new users can associate their own public key via a token. Users can run admin commands directly over SSH or through an interactive configuration shell. The README lists session recording in ttyrec format, an audit log, session and tunnel logging, and backup/restore via JSON export. Data is stored in SQLite by default or MySQL for running multiple stateless instances. It also has a healthcheck mode and supports scp, rsync, sftp, port forwarding, ssh-agent, X11 forwarding, Git, and telnet targets.
use_cases: give students or temporary users controlled access to servers
central jump host that logs all SSH sessions
manage access to servers and routers without sharing credentials
invite multiple people to an event with pre-made accounts
record and replay terminal sessions for audit
SSH access to telnet-only devices through a bastion
notable: Transparent bastion: users need no client modification or custom .ssh/config to reach hosts
Invite-token onboarding so users attach their own public keys without sharing them manually
Session recording in ttyrec format with ttyplay replay
Stateless design; horizontal scaling possible with a shared MySQL backend
Built-in configuration shell accessible over SSH, also usable for one-off commands
caveats: Does not work with mosh (per README)
A user cannot access a host with the same name as their username
Host named 'healthcheck' cannot be accessed because it is a built-in command
Default SQLite storage is not scalable; horizontal scaling requires MySQL
keywords: log who ran what on servers
